what_it_does: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are large AI models that internally split into many specialized sub-networks ("experts"); for each input, only a small subset of experts is activated, making the model large but keeping per-input computation manageable. Running MoE inference in hardware is tricky because only a sparse, unpredictable subset of expert weights is needed at any moment, causing irregular memory-access patterns and heavy data movement. This paper proposes PIMoE, which pairs a traditional neural-network accelerator chip (an NPU — a chip purpose-built for AI math) with Processing-in-Memory (PIM — memory chips that contain small compute units so data can be processed right where it is stored, cutting the cost of shuttling data back and forth). A throttle-aware scheduler decides at runtime which operations go to the NPU and which to the PIM based on each unit's current load, keeping both busy. A dedicated hardware unit near the memory controller also translates the sparse, irregular layout of expert data into a form the NPU and PIM can each consume efficiently.
